body.statement: Can the priors obtained from \(\mathrm{def:common-marginal-prior-handle}\) be normalized and transferred to the fixed two-sample experiment so that they induce identical auxiliary laws and imply \[R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\] for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\), including the capped constant-risk regime?
body.justification: A supervised lower prior that perturbs \(P_{XA}\) is detected by the auxiliary sample, so exact marginal invariance is the essential new converse mechanism.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Appendix C.5, randomizes treatment and mass parameters in a one-sample fuzzy hypothesis; WuYang2016 provides approximation duality but not the auxiliary-invariance constraint or the two-sample normalization transfer. The two point masses in \(\mathrm{def:finite-small-instance}\) verify exact \(P_{XA}\) agreement and label-gated discrepancy in a finite experiment, but their total variation is too large to supply the all-regime frontier.
body.consumer: The lower bound prevents chart-review planning from treating unlabeled records as if they also supplied outcome-bearing moments.
